svg.title: The five visible cost lines of an apparel item-level RFID program, itemized
svg.desc: An itemized budget panel listing the five visible cost lines of an apparel RFID program. The tag itself, an ARC-certified UHF inlay, runs $0.04-0.08 per item at 1M+ volume, climbing to $0.10-0.18 under 250K units. Application costs $0.01-0.03 per garment inline at source or $0.05-0.12 retrofit at the DC. An encoding station — encoder, label printer and thermal ribbon — runs $5K-15K, with 1-3 stations per supplier DC. A tunnel reader at the shipping dock runs $15K-50K per dock and keeps chargebacks out of the P&L. EDI 856 ASN integration costs $8K-25K one-time plus $2K-8K a year in VAN fees. A footer notes that four of the five lines have nothing to do with the tag — the system around the tag is where the money goes.
svg.text: Nine cost lines — these five do most of the damage
The tag itself — ARC-certified UHF inlay
slip under 250K units and pricing climbs to $0.10–0.18
Sticking it on — inline vs retrofit
tag at source unless you enjoy paying for the privilege
1–3 stations per supplier DC; yes, the ribbon is a recurring line too
Tunnel reader at the shipping dock
the bouncer that keeps Walmart / Target chargebacks off the P&L
the line first-time budgets forget — until the first rejected shipment
Four of these five lines have nothing to do with the tag — the system around the tag is where the money goes.
